site.name: Moony
site.description: Moony is a free desktop app for keeping track of your accounts, investments and loans. Your financial data stays on your computer. For macOS, Windows and Linux.

footer.blurb: A clearer picture of your finances. Right on your computer.
footer.disclaimer: Moony is not financial, tax or investment advice. Figures depend on data from third parties and may be inaccurate.
footer.nocookies: This site sets no cookies and uses no analytics.

hero.lead: Keep track of your accounts, investments and loans. Moony keeps your financial data right on your computer.
hero.caption: The real app, with sample data
hero.alt: Dashboard with the net worth, its history and the totals of a sample profile

overview.title: See where you stand.
overview.text: Account balances, investments and the debt you still owe. One overview, built around what you want to track.
overview.alt: The totals of assets, liabilities and free cash of a sample profile, with the deadlines and reminders coming up next

import.title: Start with a bank statement.
import.text: Import a statement to see where your money goes and how much is left. Organise transactions into categories and set rules for next time.
bullets: Income and spending, month by month
Undo an import if you need to

bullets: Import from XTB, Trading 212, Degiro and IBKR
investments.alt: Stock analysis with time-weighted and money-weighted return, a return chart split by region and a drawdown panel

otherInstruments.title: Property, insurance and loans, too
otherInstruments.text: Bring property, insurance policies and loans into your overview. Keep their values, payments and important dates together.
otherInstruments.alt: Loan overview with outstanding balances, interest rates and a chart of debt over time

requests.title: No tracking
requests.text: No analytics or usage statistics. Prices, exchange rates and updates are checked online. Price services see the symbols you track, not your balances.

disk.title: Encrypted data
disk.text: Records and attachments are encrypted on your computer. Exported files and saved copies are unencrypted, so keep them somewhere safe.

keys.title: Backups you control
keys.text: Back up your data to a file or export it. Save your recovery key during setup so you can reset a forgotten password.

assistant.title: Connect an AI assistant to your finances
assistant.text: Claude or another MCP client can read and change your data through a local server. The client processes it, usually in its provider's cloud.
assistant.detail: An optional feature for advanced users. Before enabling it, check how your chosen AI client handles data. You do not need an AI assistant to use Moony.
setupSteps: In Moony, open Settings → Integrations and enable AI Assistant (MCP Server).
Copy the connection command from settings. It includes your personal access token; keep it private.
Keep Moony running and unlocked while using the integration.

install.title: Install and first launch
install.unsigned: Moony is in beta. The installers do not yet have macOS and Windows code-signing certificates, so your system may show a security warning on first launch. Follow the instructions for your system below. In-app updates are verified with the project’s signing key.

mac.terminal: Open **Terminal** (Applications → Utilities) and run this once:
mac.why: It removes the “downloaded from the internet” mark that makes macOS say “Moony is damaged and can't be opened” (Gatekeeper). Then open Moony as usual.
mac.alt: If macOS instead says it cannot verify the developer, you can also go to **System Settings → Privacy & Security** (on macOS 12 and earlier: **System Preferences → Security & Privacy**), scroll to **Security** and click **Open Anyway** next to Moony.

win.keep: Download the installer. If the browser says the file is not commonly downloaded, keep it (in Edge: **⋯ → Keep → Show more → Keep anyway**).
win.run: Run it. Windows SmartScreen may show “Windows protected your PC”. Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**.

linux.fuse: Some distributions need the `libfuse2` package for AppImages.

first.title: First run
first.intro: The setup wizard will walk you through:
steps: Your **recovery key**. Save it: it is the only way to reset a forgotten password, and it works only together with the key files in the data folder, so back up your data too (**Settings → Data and backups**).
An offer to add your first account and import a bank statement.
first.outro: The dashboard then shows a Getting started checklist.

updating.title: Updating
updating.text: After you unlock Moony, it asks GitHub whether a newer version exists and offers a one-click update. The download is verified against the project's public key before it is installed. You can switch the automatic check off in **Settings**; what it sends is listed on the [Privacy page](privacy).

requirements.title: System requirements
requirements.mac: Apple Silicon and Intel Macs. The release does not state a minimum macOS version; current and recent versions are expected to work. If Moony does not open on an older one, [tell us in GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/fiiles/Moony/discussions).
requirements.win: Windows 10 and 11, 64-bit. Moony needs the Microsoft Edge WebView2 runtime, which is preinstalled on both; the installer fetches it if it is missing.
requirements.linux: x86_64 only: an AppImage, a `.deb` for Debian and Ubuntu and an `.rpm` for Fedora and openSUSE.

free.a: Yes: Moony is open source under the AGPL-3.0 licence, with no trial and no account.

warning.q: Why does my computer warn me when I open it?
warning.a: Moony is in beta and the installers do not yet have macOS and Windows code-signing certificates. Your system may show a security warning on first launch. You can find the steps on the download page. In-app updates are verified with the project’s signing key.

data.q: Does Moony collect any data about me?
data.a: No: the app has no analytics, crash reports or usage statistics. Its only requests are for prices, exchange rates and the update check, listed in full on the Privacy page.

password.q: What if I forget my password?
password.a: Use the 24-character recovery key Moony showed you at setup; it is the only way to reset a password. If you lose both, nobody can open your data, so keep a backup (Settings → Data and backups).

devices.q: Can I use Moony on my phone or another computer?
devices.a: Moony runs on macOS, Windows and Linux today, with one profile per computer and no sync. You can move your data to another computer with a backup file.

bank.q: Does it connect to my bank?
bank.a: Not directly: import statements exported from your bank as CSV, CAMT.053, MT940, OFX/QFX or QIF.

gettingStarted.title: You can start with one account.
gettingStarted.text: There is no need to add everything at once. Bring in other accounts and investments whenever you are ready.
